G8902.definition: to go out for foraging  , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8903.definition:
1.  a foraging, a foraging expedition, foray  , (Xenophon Historicus): in  plural ,  foraging parties  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  an elephant's trunk  , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. = προ-νομία, (Lucian) (ML)

G8904.definition:
1.  an opening   or  introduction to   a thing; in Music,  a prelude, overture  , (Pindar); in poems and speeches,  a proem, preface, preamble, introduction  , Lat.  exordium , (Pindar) 
2.  metaphorically  of  any prelude   or  beginning  , φροίμιον χορεύσομαι (Aeschulus Tragicus); μηδέπω ' ν προοιμίοις only just  beginning  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εἴ τι τοῦδε φρ. ματᾷ if any part of this  presage   be vain, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. generally,  a hymn  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8906.definition:
reckless haste, vehemence, rashness, indiscretion  , (Demosthenes Orator), etc. 
from προπετής (ML)

G8907.definition:
1.  to fall   or  throw oneself forward  , as in rowing, προπεσόντες ἔρεσσον, like Lat.  incumbere remis , (Odyssey by Homer):—;of suppliants,  to fall prostrate  , (Euripides) 
2.  to rush forward, rush headlong  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3.  to move forwards, advance before   the rest, (Polybius Historicus):  to project  , (Polybius Historicus) 
4. προπίτνω  poetry  for προπίπτω 
5.  to fall prostate  , ἐς γᾶν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8908.definition: in  plural , like προπύλαια, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; in  singular , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   (ML)

G8909.definition: a going up, ascent  , κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις  ascent by means of   ladders, i. e.  scaling   ladders, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. (Euripides); τειχέων πρ.  a place where   they  may be approached  , (Euripides); δωμάτων πρ. i. e.  the steps leading   to the house, (Euripides) (ML)

G8911.definition:
1.  to strike   or  dash against  , τί τινι (Iliad by Homer); ἀψῖδα πέτρῳ πρ.  letting   it  dash against  , (Euripides); τὸν πρὶν ὄλβον ἕρματι πρ.  to wreck   his happiness on a rock, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. θηρία τινί  to set   them  on   him, (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. δόρυ τινί (Euripides):—;without any notion of violence,  to put to, apply  , μαλακὰν χέρα πρ. [ ἕλκει] of a surgeon, (Pindar); πρ. παρειὰν παρηίδι (Euripides); ὄμματα τέκνοις (Euripides) 
2.  to assign to, procure for  , κέρδος τινί (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. Λακεδαιμονίοις Ὀλυμπιάδα  to give   them  the honour of   an Olympic victory, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. κακὸν τῇ πόλει (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὔκλειαν σαυτῇ (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. δεῖμά τινι, Lat.  incutere timorem alicui , (Euripides) 
3. with  accusative  of the object struck, ἀρούρας προσβάλλειν, of the Sun,  to strike   the earth  with   his rays, (Homer); of smells, βροτοῦ [ ὀσμὴ] με προσέβαλε (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4.  metaphorically   to attend to   a thing or  to add  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. μή μ᾽ ἀνάγκῃ προσβάλῃς τάδ᾽ εἰκαθεῖν  do   not  drive   me by force to give way, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6.  intransitive   to strike against, to make an attack   or  assault upon  , τινί (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; πρὸς τὸ τεῖχος (Herdotus Historicus):—; absolute   to attack, charge  , (Herdotus Historicus); προσβαλὼν αἱρεῖ τὴν πόλιν  by assault  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
7.  to put in   with a ship, ἐς τὸν λιμένα (Thucydides); πρὸς Τάραντα (Thucydides); with  dative , Σικελίᾳ (Thucydides) 
8. Mid.  to throw oneself upon, attack  , τινα (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8916.definition: to look at, behold  , (Mimnermus Lyricus), etc.; compare  aorist2   προσεῖδον:—;so in Mid., προσορωμένα (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8917.definition:
1.  to speak to   one,  to address, accost  , (Homer), etc.; πρ. ὀνόματί τινα (Demosthenes Orator):—;with  double   accusative , τί προσείπω ς᾽ ἔπο; (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  to address as   so and so, πρ. τινὰ ὡς ἀλλότριον (Plato Philosophus); πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν  to bid   him  greeting  , (Euripides) 
3.  to call   so and so,  to name  , τί νιν προσείπ; (Aeschulus Tragicus); τοῦτο γάρ ς᾽ ἔχω μόνον προσειπεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus); ὅν μοι προσεῖπας πόσιν whom  thou didst name   my husband, (Euripides) (ML)

G8920.definition: over and above, besides  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8922.definition:
1.  soft, gentle, kindly  , (Pindar); προσηνές τι λέγειν (Thucydides) 
2. with  dative , λύχνῳ προσηνές, i. e.  suitable   for burning, (Herdotus Historicus) (For derivation, see. ἀπηνής).  
3.  adverb  -νῶς, (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8924.definition:
1.  a putting to, application   of ladders to a wall, (Thucydides); of the cupping-glass, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2.  an adding, addition  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8926.definition: to set on fire   or  burn besides  :—;Pass., σκεύη προσκεκαυμένα pots  burnt at the fire  , (Aristophanes Comicus):  metaphorically , προσκαίεσθαί τινι  to be in love with . .  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8927.definition:
1.  to leave besides as a legacy  , ἀρχήν τινι (Thucydides) 
2.  to lose besides  , τὰ αὑτῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8929.definition:
1.  to be placed   or  laid by   or  upon, to lie by   or  upon  , οὔατα προσέκειτο handles  were upon   it, (Iliad by Homer); τῇ θύρᾳ προσκεῖσθαι  to keep close to   the door, (Aristophanes Comicus); δοκοὶ τῷ τείχει προσκείμεναι  lying near   the wall, (Thucydides):—; ὁ προσκείμενος ἵππος  the inside   horse (turning a corner), (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2.  to lie beside, cling to  , (Sophocles Tragicus): of a woman,  to be given to wife  , τινί (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. generally,  to be involved in   or  bound up with   good or evil, with  dative , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4.  to be attached   or  devoted to  , τινί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρ. τῷ λεγομένῳ  to put faith in   a story, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. οἴνῳ  to be addicted to   wine, (Herdotus Historicus); ἄγραις hunting, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
5.  to press upon, be urgent with   a person, with  dative , (Herdotus Historicus); προσκείμενος  with zeal  , (Thucydides) 
6. in military sense,  to press close   or  hard, pursue closely  , τινί (Thucydides);  absolute   to follow close  , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ προσκείμενον  the enemy  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. with a thing for the subject,  to fall to, belong to  , τοῖσι θεῶν τιμὴ αὕτη προσκέαται (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. τινι δοῦλος (Euripides):—;  to be laid upon   as a charge, to do something, with  infinitive , (Herdotus Historicus) 
8.  to be added   or  attached to  , (Sophocles Tragicus):—; absolute , ἡ χάρις προσκείσεται (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8931.definition:
1.  to strike against  , τινί (Plato Philosophus): absolute   to stumble, fail  , (Plutarch) 
2.  to have a collision with   another,  give offence  , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. τινί (Plutarch) 
3.  to take offence at, be angry with  , τινί (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: —; absolute   to take offence  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8932.definition:
1. Dep.: 
2.  to reckon   or  count in addition to  , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus) 
3.  to impute  , τί τινι (Plutarch) (ML)

G8935.definition:
1.  a going   or  coming to, an approach  , ἡ πρ. μάλιστα ταύτῃ ἐγένετο  the approach   was most feasible on this part, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπείπατο τὴν πρ. rejected his  advances  , (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. μελάθρων  approach to   the halls, (Euripides) 
2.  an onset  , πρόσοδοι τῆς μάχης  onsets   or  attacks  , (Euripides) 
3. like πομπή II,  a solemn procession   to a temple with singing and music, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4.  the coming forward   of a speaker  in a public assembly  , γράφεσθαι πρόσοδον to petition for  a hearing  , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς τὸν δῆμον (Aeschines Orator) 
5.  income, rent  , as opposite to principal, (Demosthenes Orator); often in  plural , (Isaeus Orator) 
6. of the public revenue, φόρων πρόσοδος (Herdotus Historicus); χρημάτων πρ. (Thucydides); mostly in  plural   the returns, revenue  , Lat.  reditus , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8936.definition: intransitive   to smell of, be redolent of  , with  genitive , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8939.definition:
1.  appearance, aspect, mien  , (Pindar);  periphrastic , σὴ πρ. thy  presence  , i. e.  thyself  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2.  a seeing, beholding, sight, view  , (Euripides) (ML)

G8940.definition:
1.  to play   or  sport with  , τινί (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  absolute   to sport, jest  , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with  accusative , πρ. θεούς  to sing to   the gods, ὕμνον πρ. τὸν Ἔρωτα  sang   a hymn  in praise of   Eros, (Plato Philosophus) 
4.  to banter  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8941.definition: to sprinkle on   one, τινί τι (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G8943.definition: an ordinance, command  , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἐκ προστάγματος (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8945.definition:
1.  one who stands before, a front-rank-man  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  a chief, leader   of a party, (Herdotus Historicus); ὁ πρ. τοῦ δήμου (Thucydides) 
3. generally,  a president, ruler  , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; προστάται τῆς εἰρήνης its  chief authors  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4.  one who stands before, a protector, guard, champion  , πυλωμάτων (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
5. at Athens, of  a citizen who took care of the   μέτοικοι, as the Rom.  patronus   took care of his  clientes;   προστάτην γράφεσθαί τινα to choose as one's  patron  , (Aristophanes Comicus); but, γράφεσθαι προστάτου to enter oneself  by one's patron's name  , attach oneself to  a patron  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. προστάτης θεοῦ  one who stands before   a god to entreat him,  a suppliant  , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8948.definition:
a deposit made by water  , πρ. Νείλου, of the Delta of the Nile, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
from προσχώννυ_μι (ML)

G8949.definition:
1.  to go to, approach  , with  dative , (Herdotus Historicus);  absolute , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  to come   or  go over to, come in, join  , τινί or πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus), attic;  absolute , (Thucydides); also, πρ. ἐς ὁμολογίαν or ὁμολογίᾳ (Herdotus Historicus) 
3.  to accede   to an opinion, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. λόγοις τινός (Sophocles Tragicus):  to make concessions  , (Euripides) 
4.  to approach  , i. e.  to agree with, be like  , τινί or πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus) 
5.  to put faith in, believe  , τινί (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

1.  the foremost   or  upper part of anything: a bust   or  half-figure  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina

G8953.definition:
1. Dep.: 
2.  to set up as a pretext   or  excuse, allege by way of excuse, plead in excuse  , with  accusative , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; with  infinitive   to allege as an excuse that . .  , (Demosthenes Orator):—; absolute   to make excuses  , (Thucydides):—;aor1 προφασισθῆναι in  passive  sense,  to be used as a pretext  , (Thucydides) 
3.  to allege   (by way of accusation)  that  , (Plato Philosophus) 
from πρόφᾶσις (ML)

G8955.definition: a guard in front;   in  plural   outposts, videttes, piquets  , (Xenophon Historicus); in  singular , ἡ πρ. αὐτοῦ his  advanced   guard, (Xenophon Historicus); διὰ προφυλακῆς with  an advanced guard  , (Thucydides) (ML)

an advanced guard  : οἱ προφύλακες 
= αἱ προφυλακαί, (Thucydides) (ML)

G8957.definition: to keep guard before, to guard   a place or house, with  accusative , (Homeric Hymns) (in the epic 2nd  plural   imperative  προφύλαχθε, for προφυλάσσετε); (Xenophon Historicus); προφυλάσσειν ἐπί τινι  to keep guard over   a person or place, (Herdotus Historicus):—; absolute   to be on guard, keep watch  , ἡ προφυλάσσουσα (i.e. ναῦς); = προφυλακίς, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Mid.  to guard oneself, to be on one's guard, take precautions  , (Herdotus Historicus):—;with  accusative   to be on one's guard   or  take precautions against  , Lat.  cavere , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8958.definition:
1.  at hand, ready  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of a drawn sword or knife, (Sophocles Tragicus); λίθοις καὶ . . ἀκοντίοις, ὡς ἕκαστός τι πρόχειρον εἶχε (Thucydides); ὃ προχειρότατον ἔχω εἰπεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. πρόχειρόν [ ἐστι] it is  easy  , with  infinitive , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. of persons,  ready   to do, with  infinitive , (Sophocles Tragicus); with  dative , πρ. τῇ φυγῇ  ready for   flight, (Euripides) 
4.  adverb  -ρως,  off-hand, readily  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8960.definition:
1.  lately, just now  , Lat.  nuper , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2.  the day before yesterday  , οὐ χθές, ἀλλὰ πρ. (Thucydides); πρώην τε καὶ χθές till  yesterday or the day before  , i. e.  till very lately  , (Herdotus Historicus); so, χθές τε καὶ πρώην (Aristophanes Comicus); πρώην καὶ χθές (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8962.definition:
the officer in command at the bow, the look-out man  , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
 (ML)

G8967.definition:
1.  first-born, firstling  , (Iliad by Homer); φοῖνιξ πρ.  first-created  , (Euripides) 
2. of rank, πρ. οἶκοι  high-born   houses, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3.  first-ordained  , (Lucian) (ML)

G8969.definition: to give a right of first-born

G8973.definition: to stomp; catch by a heel

G8975.definition:
1. mostly in  plural   feathers  , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; in  singular   a feather  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. = πτέρυξ,  a bird's wing  , in  plural   wings  , (Homer); Παλλάδος ὑπὸ πτεροῖς ὄντας,  metaphorically  from chickens under the hen's wings, (Aeschulus Tragicus): —; τῷ πτερὰ γίγνετο he got as it were  wings  , i. e. spirit, courage, (Iliad by Homer) 
3.  the wings   of a bat (see. πτίλον II), (Herdotus Historicus) 
4.  any winged creature  , as the Sphinx, (Euripides); a beetle, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. like οἰωνός, Lat.  avis , an augury, omen, (Pindar) 
6.  anything like wings  : as 
7.  a ship's wings  , i. e.  oars   (compare πτερόω); ἐρετμά, τά τε πτερὰ νηυσὶ πέλονται (Odyssey by Homer); νηὸς πτερά (Hesiod):—; hence birds are said πτεροῖς ἐρέσσειν, (Euripides) 
8. ἀέθλων πτερά, i. e.  the wings   of victory, which lift the Poet to heaven, (Pindar) 
9.  a feathered arrow  , (Euripides) 
10. τοῦ πώγωνος τὰ πτερά  the points   of the beard, (Lucian) 
11. in Architecture, of  the rows of columns along the sides   of Greek temples, see. ἄπτερος. (ML)

G8977.definition: attic -ττομαι,  future  ξομαι, Dep.  to clap the wings   like a cock crowing, (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8978.definition:
1.  feathered  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2.  winged  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. πτερωτοί (i.e. ὄρνιθες);  feathered fowl, birds  , (Euripides) (ML)

G8979.definition:
1.  to frighten, scare, alarm  , Lat.  terrere , (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  intransitive   to crouch   or  cower down for fear   (compare πτώσσω), properly of animals, (Sophocles Tragicus); of men, (Pindar), attic; πτ. βωμὸν ὕπο (Euripides); also with  accusative  loci, πτ. βωμόν  to flee cowering to   the altar, (Euripides) 
3.  to crouch   like a wild beast ready to spring, (Euripides);—;so of men in ambush, ὑπὸ τεύχεσι πεπτηῶτες (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. with  accusative  rei,  to crouch for fear of  , ἀπειλάς (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8985.definition:
1.  white-rump  , the name of a kind of antelope, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  the white-tailed eagle, the erne  , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G8986.definition:
1.  the hollow bottom   or  stand of a cup  , Lat.  fundus , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. of the sea,  the bottom, depth  , (Hesiod), etc. 
3.  the bottom   or  foundation   of a thing, in  plural , χθόνα ἐκ πυθμένων κραδαίνειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐκ π. ἔκλινε κλῇθρα (Sophocles Tragicus); δίκας π.  the anvil-stand   on which is forged the sword of retribution, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4.  the bottom, stock, root of a tree  , (Odyssey by Homer):—; metaphorically   the stem   or  stock   of a family, (Aeschulus Tragicus); σμικροῦ γένοιτ᾽ ἂν σπέρματος π. μέγας, i. e. great things might come from small, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
 (ML)

G8987.definition:
1.  to make close, cover   or  wrap up, enwrap  , (Iliad by Homer); π. νῆα λίθοισι  to surround   a ship with stones,  so as to protect   it when laid up, (Hesiod):—;  to cover thickly  , of a youth's chin, (Odyssey by Homer); πυκ. στεφάνοις  to cover thick   with crowns, (Euripides); so in Mid., στεφάνοις κεφαλὰς πυκασώμεθα [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina  ; also without στεφάνοις,  to crown, deck with garlands  , (Euripides):—;Pass., στέμμασι πυκασθείς (Herdotus Historicus); δάφνῃ πυκασθείς (Euripides);  perfect   participle  πεπυκασμένος,  thickly covered  , ὄρος πεπυκασμένον a hill  well-clothed   with wood, (Hesiod):—;Mid., πυκάζου  cover thyself  , (Euripides) 
2.  metaphorically , Ἕκτορα ἄχος πύκασε φρένας  threw a shadow over   his heart, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., νόον πεπυκασμένος,  close, cautious   of mind, (Hesiod) 
3.  to close, shut, shut up  , ἐντὸς πυκάζειν σφέας αὐτούς  to shut   themselves  close up   within, (Odyssey by Homer); πύκαζε (i.e. τὸ δῶμα);  shut   it  close  , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8988.definition: a gate-keeper, warder, porter   (see. πυλαωρός); (Aeschulus Tragicus); also as  feminine , ἡ π. δωμάτων γυνή (Euripides):—; metaphorically , τοῖον πυλωρὸν φύλακα τροφῆς such a  watchful   guardian of thy life, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8989.definition:
a tablet of box-wood  , (Lucian) 
from πυξίς (ML)

G8992.definition: mostly in  plural   pieces of wood  , rubbed one against another to produce fire, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

G8993.definition: or -καυτος,  burnt in fire  , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8994.definition: wheat  , (Homer); also in  plural , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G8998.definition:
1.  to light up, kindle  , πυρσεύσας σέλας Εὐβοίαν  having lit up   Euboea with beacon-fires  σέλας combining with the notion of the Verb), (Euripides) 
2.  to make signals by torches   or  beacon-fires  , (Xenophon Historicus):  metaphorically , πυρσεύετε κραυγὴν ἀγῶνος  give   a shout  in signal   of battle, (Euripides):—;Pass., δόξα ὥσπερ ἀπὸ σκοπῆς πυρσεύεται (Plutarch):  impersonal , πυρσεύεται  fire-signals are made  , (Lucian) (ML)

G8999.definition:
1.  a firebrand, torch  , (Iliad by Homer):—;in  plural   fires  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina  :—; metaphorically , πυρσὸς ὕμνων (Pindar);  plural   the fires of love  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2.  a beacon   or  signal-fire, bale-fire  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3.  plural  πύρσα,  watch-fires  , (Euripides) (ML)
